bug_description.normalized: While HarfBuzz subsets the staged OpenType/CFF1 font, `subr_subsetter_t::subset()` pulls attacker-controlled glyph charstrings from the font and stores operator byte slices as `parsed_cs_op_t::str`. `encode_charstrings()` then grows `str_buff_vec_t subset_charstrings`, and vulnerable `hb_vector_t<CFF::str_buff_t>::resize()` manufactures each appended `str_buff_t` by raw `memset` even though `str_buff_t` is itself `hb_vector_t<unsigned char, 1>` with embedded inline storage. Later `encode_str()` calls `buff.init()` on one of those byte-created elements, and earlier output in that same `encode_str()` first grows the nested `hb_vector_t<unsigned char, 1u>` through `alloc()`'s `!arrayZ_` branch, making it heap-backed. On the later crashing `encoder.copy_str(opstr.str)` append, the same `buff` re-enters `alloc()`'s `realloc` path at `hb-vector.hh:173`, which the saved MSAN trace records as the origin, and the following `resize()` `memset` at `hb-vector.hh:194` reports `use-of-uninitialized-value`. The fix removes `hb_vector_t`'s inline `static_array`, so vectors are no longer raw-created with embedded inline-storage state.

source.function: CFF::subr_subsetter_t<cff1_subr_subsetter_t, CFF::Subrs<OT::IntType<unsigned short, 2u> >, OT::cff1::accelerator_subset_t const, CFF::cff1_cs_interp_env_t, cff1_cs_opset_subr_subset_t>::subset
source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that materializes attacker-controlled CFF1 charstring bytes for one subset glyph.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is an attacker-controlled OpenType font. During `hb_subset()`'s CFF1 subsetting path, this line fetches the glyph's byte span from the font-backed `CharStrings` INDEX and hands it to the subroutine subsetter/interpreter.
source.note: The later sink copies slices derived from this same `byte_str_t`.

root_cause.description: Growing `str_buff_vec_t` creates new `str_buff_t` elements by raw zeroing instead of C++ construction, even though each element is itself `hb_vector_t<unsigned char, 1>` with embedded inline storage.
root_cause.note: `CFF::str_buff_t` is `typedef hb_vector_t<unsigned char, 1> str_buff_t;` at `src/hb-ot-cff-common.hh:64`. `encode_str()` later calls `buff.init()` on the chosen `buffArray[i]`, but that only rewrites `length`, `allocated`, and `arrayZ_` on the same byte-created object. The fix removes `hb_vector_t`'s `static_array`, so this raw growth no longer manufactures nested vectors with inline storage that should have been constructed.

sink.description: MSAN crash site while a later `copy_str()` append extends the same already-heap-backed per-charstring byte buffer.
sink.note: Both `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` report `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at this exact line in `hb_vector_t<unsigned char, 1u>::resize(int)`.

parser_admitted.description: The attacker-controlled font has already been recognized as a CFF1 table and control is entering the dedicated CFF1 subsetter that later reaches `encode_charstrings()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Stores each parsed operator's font-backed byte slice as `parsed_cs_op_t::str`, which later becomes `opstr.str` in the crashing `encoder.copy_str()` call.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Derived from the attacker-controlled charstring byte span loaded at `hb-subset-cff-common.hh:666`.

coarse_trace.summary: Subset parsing pulls attacker-controlled CFF1 charstrings from the font and records per-operator `byte_str_t` slices in `parsed_charstrings`.
The encoder prepares `subset_charstrings` and grows `str_buff_vec_t` to one destination buffer per subset glyph.
That growth path raw-zeroes new `str_buff_t` elements, manufacturing nested vector objects without proper construction.

coarse_trace.summary: For one chosen `buffArray[i]`, `encode_str()` reinitializes the same byte-created `str_buff_t`, then earlier output in that same call grows it past its one-byte inline capacity.
The first inner growth after `buff.init()` takes `alloc()`'s `!arrayZ_` branch and installs heap storage for that same `buff`.
A later `copy_str()` append on the same `buff` re-enters `alloc()`'s `realloc` origin and then reaches the `resize()` sink where MSAN reports `use-of-uninitialized-value`.

fine_trace.function: CFF::subr_subsetter_t<cff1_subr_subsetter_t, CFF::Subrs<OT::IntType<unsigned short, 2u> >, OT::cff1::accelerator_subset_t const, CFF::cff1_cs_interp_env_t, cff1_cs_opset_subr_subset_t>::subset
fine_trace.note: For one subset glyph, the CFF subsetter reads the font-backed `CharStrings` entry into `str`; this byte span is the raw attacker-controlled charstring later sliced into `parsed_cs_op_t::str` records.
When interpretation finishes one operator span, `add_op()` stores that exact font-backed subspan as `val->str`. Later `encode_str()` reuses these stored slices as `opstr.str`.

Before re-encoding, `encode_charstrings()` sizes `buffArray` to the subset glyph count. The first harness `trySubset()` already passes 19 codepoints, so this growth exceeds `hb_vector_t<str_buff_t>`'s two-element inline capacity.

Inside that growth, `hb_vector_t` byte-zeroes each appended `str_buff_t` with `memset`. Because `str_buff_t` is itself `hb_vector_t<unsigned char, 1>` and vulnerable `hb_vector_t` still embeds `static_array`, these destination objects are created as raw bytes rather than by their constructors.

fine_trace.function: CFF::subr_subsetter_t<cff1_subr_subsetter_t, CFF::Subrs<OT::IntType<unsigned short, 2u> >, OT::cff1::accelerator_subset_t const, CFF::cff1_cs_interp_env_t, cff1_cs_opset_subr_subset_t>::encode_str
fine_trace.note: Before re-encoding this charstring, `encode_str()` reinitializes the chosen destination buffer: `length=0`, `allocated=ARRAY_LENGTH(static_array)` (1), and `arrayZ_=nullptr`. The destination is still the same `buffArray[i]` element manufactured by step 4; this step only rewrites its scalar fields.

fine_trace.function: CFF::subr_subsetter_t<cff1_subr_subsetter_t, CFF::Subrs<OT::IntType<unsigned short, 2u> >, OT::cff1::accelerator_subset_t const, CFF::cff1_cs_interp_env_t, cff1_cs_opset_subr_subset_t>::encode_str
fine_trace.note: After step 5, every source-level site that can emit bytes into this charstring buffer lies in this prefix/loop block. The staged artifacts do not identify which exact earlier branch fired before the crash, but reaching the later `realloc` branch proves one of these earlier emissions already appended enough bytes to push this same `buff` past its one-byte inline capacity.

On the first growth past capacity after step 5, `alloc()` takes the `!arrayZ_` arm, heap-allocates `new_array`, copies any already-emitted inline bytes from `static_array`, and then installs that heap buffer into `arrayZ_`. This is the missing state transition that makes the same `buff` heap-backed before the later crashing append.

fine_trace.function: CFF::subr_subsetter_t<cff1_subr_subsetter_t, CFF::Subrs<OT::IntType<unsigned short, 2u> >, OT::cff1::accelerator_subset_t const, CFF::cff1_cs_interp_env_t, cff1_cs_opset_subr_subset_t>::encode_str
fine_trace.note: Later in the same `encode_str()` loop, the current `opstr` again reaches the default arm and forwards its stored font slice into `copy_str()`. This is the `encode_str` frame on the saved crash stack.
`copy_str()` captures the current output length as `offset` and asks the nested `hb_vector_t<unsigned char, 1>` buffer to grow to `offset + str.length` for this operator slice.
For the current append, `alloc()` now reaches the `arrayZ_`-nonnull branch and extends the already-heap-backed buffer with `realloc`; the saved MSAN origin names this exact line.
MSAN crash site. Returning from step 10, `resize()` immediately executes this tail-clearing `memset` for the current append and reports `use-of-uninitialized-value`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partial - the source-level root cause is step 4's raw byte construction of `str_buff_t` elements. The repaired trace now records the missing inner transition as step 7's `!arrayZ_` allocation/install on the same `buff`, while the saved MSAN allocation context is the later step 10 `realloc` on that already-heap-backed object.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes - fine-trace steps 8 through 11 map directly to the saved MSAN crash/origin chain, and steps 1 through 7 record the earlier source-level transitions, including the first inner allocation that makes step 10's `realloc` reachable.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch rewrites `hb_vector_t` to remove `Type static_array[PreallocedCount]`, switch `arrayZ()` to the heap pointer only, and initialize `allocated`/`length` from zero. That change makes `hb_vector_t` safely byte-relocatable and eliminates the nested-inline-storage condition that the saved vulnerable path depends on. This is a source-level conclusion; no fixed-runtime execution is staged in Stage 02.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: One staged vulnerable run reproduced the issue. `runtime_disambiguation` is disabled in `run_flags.json`, so this trace stays source-grounded and relies on the saved MSAN crash/origin stacks plus the fixing diff instead of any added instrumentation.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved `/bin/arvo run` executes `/out/hb-subset-fuzzer /tmp/poc` and reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `hb_vector_t<unsigned char, 1u>::resize` while subsetting the font's CFF1 table.

format.name: OpenType/CFF1 font
format.contract: The available evidence establishes only the exact staged witness font. When `/out/hb-subset-fuzzer` processes this `poc`, HarfBuzz enters the CFF1 subroutine-subsetting path, `encode_charstrings()` grows `subset_charstrings` beyond its two-element inline capacity, and a later `encode_str()` default branch executes `encoder.copy_str(opstr.str)` on one destination `str_buff_t`, leading to `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `hb_vector_t<unsigned char, 1u>::resize`. The staged artifacts do not identify which specific parsed opcode was being copied or whether the first fixed-text `trySubset()` call or the later 16-codepoint data-derived call supplied the crashing glyph list, so the contract should not be generalized beyond this witness.
